title: MXene/berberine-loaded hydrogel microneedle patches for the regeneration of infected skin wounds
content: Bacteria-infected skin wounds remain challenging to treat because persistent infection, excessive oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration create an interconnected pathological microenvironment that hinders tissue healing. Herein, we developed a multifunctional polymeric hydrogel microneedle (PHMN) platform incorporating MXene/berberine (MX/BBR) conjugates to achieve localized, near-infrared (NIR)-triggered antibacterial therapy, antioxidant protection, and tissue regeneration. The PHMNs were fabricated by photocrosslinking methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA) containing MX/BBR onto a poly(vinyl alcohol) backing layer, generating well-defined microneedle arrays with adequate mechanical strength, favorable cytocompatibility, controlled degradation, and sustained BBR release. The integration of MX/BBR conjugates into the hydrogel microneedle platform provides NIR-responsive photothermal activity and sustained BBR release, offering a multifunctional strategy for antibacterial treatment and wound repair. Upon 808 nm NIR irradiation, the constructed PHMN/MX/BBR patches exhibited potent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, while effectively protecting cells against oxidative stress and promoting cell migration and endothelial tube formation. In a S. aureus-infected full-thickness skin wound model, combined PHMN/MX/BBR treatment and NIR irradiation markedly accelerated wound closure and enhanced re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and tissue remodelling, without apparent systemic toxicity. Unlike conventional wound dressings that primarily provide passive protection or single-mode antibacterial treatment, this platform integrates localized delivery, externally activated photothermal therapy, and intrinsic antioxidant activity to simultaneously address infection, oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration. Collectively, this work establishes MX/BBR-integrated hydrogel microneedles as a multifunctional and minimally invasive strategy for the coordinated management of bacteria-infected wounds.
